source.publication: 2025 Complete Income Tax Instruction Booklet (ip25), Kansas Department of Revenue, with Form K-40 and Schedule S bound in (PDF pages 19-22)
source.section: Form K-40 lines 1-12 (ip25 PDF page 20; exemption block PDF page 19); K-40 instructions lines 1-3 (PDF page 6), line 4 and exemptions (PDF page 6), lines 5-8 (PDF page 7); WORKSHEET - Standard Deduction for People 65 or Older and/or Blind (PDF page 6); tax rate schedule: 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34) and Tax Table (PDF pages 27-34)

worked: Federal AGI = wages (spouse) 40,000.00 + private pension (you) 30,000.00 = 70,000.00. Federal taxable income = 70,000.00 - standard deduction 33,100.00 (31,500.00 + 1 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older) = 36,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Kansas starts from federal AGI). No Kansas modifications: Schedule S lines A9 and A26 are 0.00, line A27 net modification 0.00 (the K-40 instructions let a filer skip line 2). Form K-40: line 1 federal AGI 70,000.00; line 2 modifications 0.00; line 3 Kansas AGI = 70,000.00 + (0.00) = 70,000.00; line 4 standard deduction (married filing joint), worksheet for people 65 or older: 1 box checked (you only), 8,240.00 + 1 x 700.00 = 8,940.00 (the worksheet prints 8,940.00); line 5 exemption allowance (2 exemptions) 18,320.00, 0 dependents; line 6 total deductions = 8,940.00 + 18,320.00 = 27,260.00; line 7 taxable income = 70,000.00 - 27,260.00 = 42,740.00; line 8 tax (rate schedule as numbers, PDF page 34): 5.2% x 42,740.00 = 2,222.4800 = 2,222.48. Line 7 is 100,000 or less, so the form reads the tax table: row 42,701-42,750, married filing joint column, PDF page 30, gives 2,222; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 9-10 do not apply (resident); line 11 0.00; line 12 total income tax 2,222.48. Credits (lines 13-15, 17): none, 0.00; state income tax = 2,222.48. Each spouse has their own box: the younger spouse (61) gets no amount, and the older spouse's age is not extended to both. 8,940.00, not 9,640.00.
accepted_approximations: A pension from another state's government, private pensions, IRA and other employer-plan distributions and Roth conversions stay in Kansas income: no line subtracts them. This is read from the booklet's silence, not from a sentence saying they are taxed.
Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
